rules.split_rule: No split. Any tag containing 'lighting' or a luminaire noun (light, lights, lamp, pendant, downlight, spotlight, troffer, chandelier, sconce, luminaire, LED) is lighting whatever the modifier — 'exterior dusk lighting', 'facade lighting', 'recessed ceiling lighting' included. The lighting rule outranks the ceiling, material, shape and time-of-day rules; only a bare time word with no fixture ('dusk', 'night') goes to time-of-day.

Genuinely three senses; apply in order. (1) a light word present ('recessed ceiling lights', 'linear ceiling lighting', 'ceiling spotlights') -> lighting. (2) the tag names the ceiling's lining or finish ('acoustic ceiling tiles', 'timber slatted ceiling', 'exposed concrete ceiling', 'perforated acoustic ceiling', 'corrugated metal ceiling') -> material. (3) otherwise the ceiling as built form ('double-height ceiling', 'high ceiling', 'exposed ceiling', 'coffered ceiling', 'exposed ceiling ductwork') -> architectural-element. Never furniture-fittings.

No split. Every 'contemporary X' is design-style, including style+sector pairs ('contemporary corporate', 'contemporary healthcare', 'contemporary workplace') — the sector half is already on the project. Only a luminaire or furniture head noun escapes ('contemporary pendant lights' -> lighting).

Timber is a modifier; the head noun decides. Surface or lining head noun (flooring, cladding, panelling, slats, battens, decking, veneer, soffit) -> material. Loose furniture or joinery head noun (dining table, display shelving, benches, screens you could remove) -> furniture-fittings. Structural or fixed built head noun (trusses, beams, columns, louvres, pergola, staircase, balustrade) -> architectural-element.

Glass is a modifier but its head nouns are nearly always fixed built elements (balustrade, partition, curtain wall, facade, doors, windows, skylight, roof) -> architectural-element. Furniture head noun ('glass coffee table', 'glass display cabinet') -> furniture-fittings. Light fitting ('glass pendant lights') -> lighting.

Pure shape modifier — it never sets the category. Fixed built head noun (facade, partition, wall, staircase, balcony, soffit) -> architectural-element. Furniture head noun (reception counter, reception desk, bar counter, sofa, banquette) -> furniture-fittings. Light head noun ('curved cove lighting') -> lighting. Bare 'curved forms'/'curvilinear' as a design language -> design-style.

Furniture-fittings for every table (boardroom, meeting, conference, coffee, dining, side, console). Single exception: 'table lamp' and any '... lamp' -> lighting, because the head noun is the lamp, not the table.

Head noun decides. A room, area, hall or terrace ('dining room', 'restaurant dining area', 'outdoor dining terrace', 'open plan living and dining') -> space-type. A furniture piece ('dining table', 'marble dining table', 'upholstered dining chairs', 'dining banquette') -> furniture-fittings.

'Floor' as a walked-on surface or its finish ('polished concrete floor', 'terrazzo floor', 'marble floor', 'floor tiles', 'large format floor tiles') -> material, whatever the material modifier. 'floor lamp', 'floor uplighter', 'floor washer' -> lighting. 'floor-to-ceiling ...' is a different token — see its own rule.

Seating is furniture-fittings (banquette, lounge, modular, breakout, tiered, built-in bench) unless the head noun turns it into a place: '... seating area', '... seating zone', 'seating nook' -> space-type.

Metal is a modifier; the head noun decides. Surface or lining head noun (cladding, cladding panels, panels, mesh, screen, perforated sheet, ceiling lining) -> material. Discrete built element (balustrade, handrail, railing, louvres, roof, column, framework, canopy, staircase) -> architectural-element.

In this vocabulary 'linear' is almost always a luminaire form ('linear led', 'linear pendant lights', 'recessed linear lighting', 'linear ceiling lighting') -> lighting. Where the head noun is not a light, it decides normally ('linear timber slats' -> material, 'linear park' -> setting). The modifier itself never sets the category.

Head noun decides. Surface or finish head noun (floor, flooring, paving, pavement, wall finish, soffit, exposed concrete ceiling/wall, board-formed concrete) -> material. Discrete built element (columns, beams, stairs, canopy, planter, pathway, balustrade) -> architectural-element.

'Recessed' plus any luminaire (downlights, spotlights, troffer, strip, linear lighting, ceiling lights) -> lighting, which is the overwhelming majority. With a non-light head noun the head noun decides ('recessed shelving' -> furniture-fittings, 'recessed handrail' -> architectural-element).

Genuine split, and the brief fixes it. Tags that only state the viewpoint — 'exterior facade', 'building exterior', 'facade view' -> view. Every facade tag that names the built thing — 'glazed facade', 'glazing facade', 'curved glass facade', 'curtain wall facade', 'brick facade', 'geometric facade', 'floor-to-ceiling glass facade' -> architectural-element (the material word is only a modifier). 'facade lighting' -> lighting.

No split. Every cladding tag is material, including 'cladding panels', 'corrugated metal cladding', 'timber wall cladding', 'stone cladding', 'brick cladding', 'marble wall cladding'. Cladding is a finish, never an element.

Marble is a modifier; the head noun decides. Surface head noun (flooring, floor, wall cladding, feature wall, tile, countertop as a finish) -> material. Furniture head noun (coffee table, dining table, reception desk, reception counter, side table) -> furniture-fittings.

Modifier with two readings. 'Exposed' plus a building system or structure (ductwork, services, steel trusses, structure, beams, columns, soffit, ceiling) -> architectural-element. 'Exposed' plus a material read as a surface finish ('exposed brick wall', 'exposed concrete wall', 'exposed concrete ceiling') -> material. If both could apply, ask whether the tag describes what the surface is made of (material) or what part of the building is on show (architectural-element).

Head noun decides. A place ('reception lounge', 'hotel lobby lounge', 'executive lounge', 'breakout lounge', 'waiting lounge', 'lounge seating area') -> space-type. A piece of furniture ('lounge seating', 'lounge armchairs', 'lounge chairs', 'modular lounge seating') -> furniture-fittings.

Pure modifier — never sets the category on its own. Luminaire head noun (chandelier, pendant light, pendant lighting) -> lighting. Furniture or art object (armchairs, sofa, art installation, feature piece) -> furniture-fittings. Fixed built form (staircase, ceiling, column, screen, volume) -> architectural-element. Abstract head noun (architecture, modernism, form, elegance) -> design-style, which is also where bare 'sculptural' lands.

Pure modifier. Light head noun ('integrated cove lighting', 'integrated led lighting') -> lighting. Planting head noun ('integrated planters', 'integrated planter boxes', 'integrated greenery') -> sustainability, with no exception for 'box' — near-identical tags must not scatter. Joinery or seating ('integrated cabinetry', 'integrated bench seating', 'integrated joinery') -> furniture-fittings. Landscape context ('integrated landscape') -> setting.

Genuine split. Where the tag only states where the camera is — bare 'exterior', 'exterior facade', 'building exterior', 'exterior view' -> view. 'exterior lighting', 'exterior dusk lighting' -> lighting. 'Exterior' plus a place noun (entrance, walkway, plaza, courtyard, terrace) -> space-type. 'Exterior' plus a built object (signage, louvres, staircase, canopy) -> architectural-element.

'Corporate' is a sector word, so on its own it drops; paired with a style word it is design-style ('contemporary corporate', 'modern corporate', 'corporate elegance', 'sleek corporate', 'playful corporate'). With a physical head noun the object decides ('corporate signage' -> architectural-element, 'corporate art' -> furniture-fittings).
No split. Ceiling tiles, floor tiles, carpet tiles, terrazzo tiles, patterned tiles, large format tiles — all material. A tile is a finish, never an element.

'Industrial' here is a design language, not a sector: 'industrial chic', 'industrial modern', 'industrial minimalist', 'industrial accents', bare 'industrial' -> design-style. Only a concrete head noun escapes ('industrial pendant lights' -> lighting, 'industrial style shelving' -> furniture-fittings).

The modifier decides. A colour or atmosphere word in front ('warm elegance', 'moody elegance', 'dark elegance', 'muted elegance') -> colour-mood. A design-language or sector word in front ('modern elegance', 'classic elegance', 'minimalist elegance', 'corporate elegance', 'biophilic elegance', 'refined elegance', 'sophisticated elegance') -> design-style.

Head noun decides, and steel's head nouns are usually structure or metalwork (handrail, handrails, balustrade, trusses, columns, framework, structure, elevator doors, mullions) -> architectural-element. Surface or lining head noun ('steel cladding', 'stainless steel panels', 'steel mesh screen') -> material. Furniture head noun ('steel frame chairs') -> furniture-fittings.

Modifier. Place head noun (courtyard, terrace, plaza, swimming pool, lap pool, seating area, dining terrace, aquatic center) -> space-type. Furniture head noun ('outdoor furniture', 'outdoor lounge chairs') -> furniture-fittings. Where the tag is about the relationship rather than the place ('indoor-outdoor connection', 'indoor-outdoor living') -> setting. 'outdoor lighting' -> lighting.

A dimension modifier, not a category. Glazing head noun (windows, glazing, glass, glass doors, curtain wall, glass facade) -> architectural-element. Soft or loose head noun (drapery, curtains, sheer curtains, shelving, bookshelves, joinery) -> furniture-fittings.

Default material: any acoustic surface treatment (ceiling tiles, ceiling panels, wall panels, wall panelling, tile ceiling, perforated acoustic ceiling, acoustic baffles fixed to a ceiling) -> material. Loose or desk-mounted items ('acoustic desk dividers', 'acoustic screens', 'acoustic pods', 'acoustic booths') -> furniture-fittings. Do not send acoustic tags to architectural-element.

Default material: wall panels, ceiling panels, cladding panels, timber panels, fluted panels, metal cladding panels, aluminium composite panels, perforated metal panels. Two exceptions: 'solar panels' (and any energy panel) -> sustainability; panels that are really a partition or screen system ('partition panels', 'movable wall panels') -> architectural-element.

Genuine split on the head noun. Light head noun ('accent lighting', 'warm accent lighting', 'accent spotlights') -> lighting. Furniture head noun ('accent cushions', 'accent armchair', 'accent chairs', 'accent rug') -> furniture-fittings. Colour statement ('accent wall', 'red accent wall', 'blue accent wall', 'vibrant accent', 'colour accent', bare 'accent') -> colour-mood, matching the seeded example 'blue accent wall'.

'Neutral' as a palette or tonal statement ('warm neutral', 'neutral palette', 'neutral tones', 'sophisticated neutral', 'bright neutral', 'clean neutral') -> colour-mood. Only when the head noun is a physical finish does the finish win ('neutral wall finish', 'neutral carpet' -> material). Never furniture-fittings.

Three senses, resolved by what follows. (1) 'light' as a luminaire or a quality of illumination ('pendant light', 'recessed ceiling light', 'drum pendant light', 'natural light', 'daylight', 'light-filled') -> lighting. (2) 'light' as a pale-colour modifier on a material ('light wood flooring', 'light timber flooring', 'light oak veneer') -> material, because the head noun is the finish. (3) 'light' in an atmosphere phrase ('light and airy', 'light and bright') -> colour-mood.

Pure modifier. Abstract head noun or bare ('geometric', 'geometric modernism', 'geometric modern', 'bold geometric', 'clean geometric') -> design-style. Built form head noun ('geometric facade', 'geometric volume', 'geometric screen', 'geometric ceiling') -> architectural-element. Finish head noun ('geometric patterned carpet', 'geometric tile') -> material.

Any 'X architecture' is design-style — high-tech, sculptural, angular, organic, parametric, geometric, contemporary sports, urban. One exception: a green or wellness qualifier ('sustainable architecture', 'green architecture', 'passive architecture') -> sustainability. This rule outranks the 'urban' rule, so 'urban architecture' is design-style, not setting.

Split on what 'urban' qualifies. A place or context noun ('urban high-dense', 'urban commercial', 'urban streetscape', 'urban residential', 'urban waterfront', 'urban context') -> setting. A style word ('contemporary urban', 'urban modern', 'urban chic') -> design-style, by the style+sector rule. 'urban architecture' -> design-style, per the architecture rule.

Bare 'hospitality' (and 'luxury hospitality' read as a sector) -> drop: it is a sector already on the project. Every 'X hospitality' where X is a style or tone word -> design-style ('modern hospitality', 'contemporary hospitality', 'refined hospitality', 'warm hospitality', 'hospitality chic', 'elegant hospitality'), including tone words like 'warm' — the style+sector rule outranks the colour-mood reading here. Never setting.

Head noun decides. A place ('reception area', 'reception lobby', 'reception lounge', 'hotel reception') -> space-type. The joinery ('reception desk', 'reception counter', 'curved reception desk', 'marble reception desk', 'timber reception counter') -> furniture-fittings, matching the seeded example 'curved reception counter'.

Split on the head noun. Plants or greenery ('indoor plants', 'indoor potted plant(s)', 'indoor planters', 'indoor greenery', 'indoor planting', 'potted indoor plants') -> sustainability, matching the seeded 'indoor planting' — planters and planter boxes go with them, never architectural-element. A place ('indoor swimming pool', 'indoor aquatic center', 'indoor garden' as a room) -> space-type. The indoor/outdoor relationship ('indoor-outdoor connection', 'indoor-outdoor flow') -> setting.

category_verdict:
Governing principle behind almost every contested word: THE HEAD NOUN DECIDES, the modifier never does. Material, colour and shape words, and the recurring qualifiers exposed / integrated / curved / recessed / linear / sculptural / floor-to-ceiling / geometric / acoustic, only qualify a thing — the thing sets the category. Two overrides beat the head noun: any luminaire or quality of illumination goes to lighting, and any plant / planting / greenery / planter goes to sustainability. A surface finish (flooring, cladding, panelling, tiles, paving, wall or ceiling lining) is material; a discrete fixed built thing (balustrade, handrail, column, truss, canopy, louvre, partition, window, facade) is architectural-element; anything loose or removable is furniture-fittings. That single test resolves timber, glass, metal, concrete, marble, steel, curved, exposed, panels, floor-to-ceiling and acoustic without further argument.

On sizing: nothing is so wrong-sized that it should be deleted, but three buckets are doing work that belongs elsewhere. architectural-element (232, 18%) is the catch-all of last resort and is absorbing surface finishes that are material — applying the head-noun rule should take it to roughly 190. design-style (212, 17%) is inflated by bare vague adjectives the brief says to drop ('sleek', 'clean lined', 'functional design', 'modern', 'refined') and should fall to about 170. Consequently drop at 102 (8%) is too small: raw Gemini output over 35k photographs normally yields 15-20% noise, so expect 140-180 once vague style adjectives and bare sector/place words are swept out of design-style and setting. The four tiny categories are not errors of existence — view, time-of-day, medium and photography-style are closed sets by definition (view has exactly four ideas, time-of-day five), so small is correct. But time-of-day (4) and photography-style (9) are under-filled even for closed sets: dawn/day/dusk/night/golden-hour tags have leaked into lighting and colour-mood, and aerial/wide/detail-shot tags into view. Two rules fix that overlap, which the brief itself creates by listing 'aerial' under both: 'aerial view' and 'aerial photograph of the site' -> view when the tag states the vantage point, 'aerial', 'drone shot', 'wide shot', 'detail shot' -> photography-style when it states how the picture was taken; and a bare time word -> time-of-day, while the same word qualifying a fixture ('exterior dusk lighting') stays lighting. lighting (107), material (151), space-type (125) and furniture-fittings (195) are all healthy and well-used; colour-mood (46), setting (42) and sustainability (34) are small but coherent and each is the only home for its axis.
merge_or_drop: Merge nothing, drop no category. The four smallest — view (6), time-of-day (4), medium (7), photography-style (9) — are small because they are closed vocabularies, and all four are seeded axes people genuinely filter by. Their low counts are a classification leak, not evidence the category is unwanted.

architectural-element (232): not merged, but tightened. Move every '<material> cladding / panels / tiles / flooring / paving / wall finish / ceiling lining' tag to material by the head-noun rule. Expected size ~190.

design-style (212): not merged, but re-swept. Push bare vague adjectives with no design content ('sleek', 'clean lined', 'functional design', 'modern', 'nice', 'stylish') to drop; keep style+sector pairs. Expected size ~170.

drop (102) is undersized at 8%. After the design-style sweep and after bare sector words ('hospitality', 'corporate', 'showflat') and regions ('sydney', 'bangkok', 'apac', 'australia') are pulled out of design-style and setting, expect 140-180.

sustainability (34) has a coherence problem, not a size problem. Keep biophilic design, greenery/indoor planting/planters, green certification, heritage adaptive reuse, solar. Drop the strays that merely sound institutional ('institutional standard', and 'smart building' wherever it is not an observable attribute) rather than merging the category away.

setting (42): keep, but it must never become the home for regions — a place name is drop, not setting. Its legitimate content is context and density: urban high-dense, coastal, waterfront, urban commercial, indoor-outdoor connection, integrated landscape.

photography-style (9) and time-of-day (4): under-filled, fix by reclaiming rather than by inventing anything new — aerial/wide/detail/lifestyle/documentary back from view and design-style, bare dawn/day/dusk/night/golden hour back from lighting and colour-mood.

colour-mood (46) and lighting (107) overlap only at 'warm' — settle it once: 'warm lighting' and 'warm accent lighting' are lighting (a fixture or its output), 'warm neutral', 'warm tones', 'warm sophisticated', 'warm elegance' are colour-mood.
